acneiform_rash_grade.label: Current cetuximab skin toxicity grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No acneiform rash.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Papules/pustules covering under 10% body-surface area, with or without pruritus or tenderness.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Papules/pustules covering 10-30% body-surface area with or without symptoms and psychosocial/instrumental-ADL impact, or over 30% with mild symptoms.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Papules/pustules covering over 30% body-surface area with moderate/severe symptoms, limiting self-care ADL, or local superinfection requiring oral antibiotics.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening consequences, or extensive superinfection requiring IV antibiotics.

acneiform_rash_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade by body-surface area, symptoms, psychosocial impact and impact on activities of daily living.

skin_delay_weeks.label: Weeks withheld for this skin episode

skin_failed_recovery.label: Skin reaction failed to recover within the source withholding period

infusion_reaction_grade.label: Cetuximab infusion reaction grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No infusion-related or hypersensitivity reaction.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Mild transient reaction; interruption of the infusion is not indicated; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Infusion interruption or treatment is indicated, with prompt response to symptomatic medication; prophylaxis may be needed for 24 hours or less.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Prolonged symptoms not rapidly responsive to treatment/brief interruption, or recurrence after initial improvement; hospitalisation indicated for clinical sequelae.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

infusion_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade by required interruption, response to symptomatic treatment, recurrence, hospitalisation and life-threatening features.

reaction_first_15_minutes.label: Reaction in first 15 minutes of first cetuximab infusion

ocular_symptoms.label: New eye pain, redness, light sensitivity or blurred vision

lowest_anc.label: Lowest ANC during delayed weeks / previous toxicity

lowest_platelets.label: Lowest platelets during delayed weeks / previous toxicity

other_nonhaem_toxicity_grade.label: Current other non-haematological toxicity grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No other non-haematological adverse event.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Grade 1 under the named CTCAE term: generally mild or asymptomatic, with observation only and no intervention indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Grade 2 under the named CTCAE term: generally moderate; local/non-invasive intervention may be indicated and instrumental activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Grade 3 under the named CTCAE term: severe or medically significant; hospital care may be indicated and self-care activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Grade 4 under the named CTCAE term: life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

other_nonhaem_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify the exact adverse event and use its toxicity-specific CTCAE definition; assess symptoms, intervention and functional impact before selecting the grade.

diarrhoea_grade.label: Current diarrhoea grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No increase above the patient's usual stool frequency or ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Increase of fewer than 4 stools per day above baseline, or mild increase in ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools per day above baseline, or moderate increase in ostomy output; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Increase of 7 or more stools per day above baseline, incontinence, hospital care indicated, or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade using increase in stools over baseline, ostomy output, need for hospitalisation and impact on self-care; do not grade from the word “diarrhoea” alone.

options.description: No oral mucositis.

options.description: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate

eligibility: Indication as listed in the current official NCCP regimen
Performance status and organ function appropriate for the selected treatment
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding where prohibited by the current source
monitoring: FBC, renal and liver profile as specified by the current NCCP regimen
Treatment-specific toxicity monitoring before each administration/cycle
dose_modifications: Use source-mapped component rules below. Relative reductions require the actual current component dose level; do not assume level 0. Source ambiguities require consultant/pharmacy clarification.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Risk assigned from the most emetogenic active component and treatment phase.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for moderate emetogenic risk
supportive_care.premedication: Cetuximab antihistamine plus corticosteroid at least one hour before infusion, including subsequent infusions; follow local policy. Antiemetics per NCCP/local moderate-risk protocol. Assess prophylactic atropine suitability; separate delayed-diarrhoea plan.
other_supportive_care: Skin care, electrolyte monitoring including monthly magnesium/calcium for two months after cetuximab; eye and respiratory symptom review.
Confirm DPD result, line/pump care and fluorouracil cardiac warning symptoms.

administration.notes: First weekly dose 400 mg/m² over 120 minutes; subsequent weekly doses 250 mg/m² over 60 minutes.
Weekly cetuximab visit between chemotherapy cycles.
Given before fluorouracil; omit/delay with fluorouracil bolus.
